lessons.title: How a solar cell makes electricity
lessons.summary: Photons, electron–hole pairs and the p–n junction, animated step by step.
takeaways: A solar cell is a large p–n junction diode made of silicon.
Light frees electrons; the junction's electric field pushes them to the contacts.
The cell produces direct current (DC); an inverter converts it to AC.

lessons.title: From sand to solar panel
lessons.summary: Quartz → polysilicon → ingot → wafer → cell → module: the manufacturing journey.
takeaways: Silicon is refined from quartz sand to very high purity polysilicon.
Monocrystalline ingots are grown by the Czochralski process, then sliced into thin wafers.
Wafers are doped, coated and metallised into cells, then laminated into modules.

lessons.title: On-grid, off-grid & hybrid systems
lessons.summary: Toggle system types, simulate a power cut and watch the energy flow through the day.
takeaways: On-grid systems have no battery and switch off during outages (anti-islanding).
Off-grid systems rely entirely on batteries.
Hybrid systems combine grid export with battery backup.

lessons.title: Peak sun hours & daily generation
lessons.summary: Why a whole sunny day equals only a few 'peak' hours — and how to turn that into kWh.
takeaways: One peak sun hour = 1 kWh/m² of sunlight (1000 W/m² for one hour).
Daily energy ≈ system kWp × peak sun hours × performance ratio.
Much of South India receives roughly 4.5–5.5 peak sun hours per day on average.

lessons.title: Mono, poly, PERC, TOPCon & beyond
lessons.summary: P-type vs N-type, PERC vs TOPCon, and how module technology evolved — compared side by side.
takeaways: Monocrystalline silicon has replaced polycrystalline in most new modules.
N-type cells avoid boron–oxygen light-induced degradation and usually have better temperature coefficients.
TOPCon adds a tunnel-oxide passivated contact for higher efficiency than PERC.

lessons.title: Half-cut cells, busbars & fingers
lessons.summary: Halving the cell halves the current — see why that cuts resistive loss and helps in shade.
takeaways: Resistive loss scales with the square of current (I²R).
Half-cut cells carry half the current, cutting ribbon losses to about a quarter per cell.
Splitting the module into two halves improves tolerance to partial shading.

lessons.title: Bifacial modules & rear-side gain
lessons.summary: Light reflected from the ground adds power from the back — try the real datasheet gain table.
takeaways: Bifacial modules also convert light reaching their rear side.
Bifaciality factor = rear Pmax ÷ front Pmax (80 ± 5% for the Anchor TOPCon).
Gain depends on ground reflectivity (albedo), mounting height and row spacing.

lessons.title: Module efficiency, calculated
lessons.summary: Efficiency = power ÷ (area × 1000 W/m²). Check it yourself with real module dimensions.
takeaways: Module efficiency compares rated power with the module's total area.
Higher efficiency puts more watts on a limited roof.
Cell efficiency is higher than module efficiency because of frame, gaps and interconnection losses.

lessons.title: Degradation, PID & manufacturing defects
lessons.summary: How modules age, what PID, micro-cracks and hot spots do, and how manufacturers test against them.
takeaways: Performance warranties are linear: a first-year step, then a small yearly loss.
PID, micro-cracks, hot spots and delamination can cause serious long-term loss.
N-type TOPCon modules are generally less sensitive to LID and PID than P-type PERC.

lessons.title: How inverters work & MPPT
lessons.summary: Drag the operating point along a real module's I-V curve and find the maximum power point.
takeaways: Power = voltage × current; it peaks at the maximum power point (MPP).
MPPT continuously adjusts operating voltage to stay at the MPP.
Dual-MPPT inverters track two strings independently — useful for shade or two roof faces.

lessons.title: Reading a datasheet: Voc, Isc, Vmp, Imp
lessons.summary: Every important datasheet term decoded, with real values from our catalogue.
takeaways: Voc rises in cold weather and sets the maximum string length.
Vmp must stay within the inverter's MPPT range.
Isc is used for fuse and cable sizing; Imp for current limits.

lessons.title: DC/AC ratio & inverter clipping
lessons.summary: Why designers deliberately put more panel watts than inverter watts — and when it starts to clip.
takeaways: AC capacity is what the grid sees; DC capacity is what the modules produce.
Modest oversizing recovers energy lost to heat and low light.
Too much oversizing clips the midday peak; stay within the inverter's max PV power.

lessons.title: Tilt & orientation
lessons.summary: Tilt ≈ latitude, face south, never flat — see the effect of each choice.
takeaways: A fixed tilt close to the site latitude (about 13° in Chennai) maximises annual yield.
South-facing is best in India; east/west lose a little.
Avoid flat installation — about 10° or more helps rain clean the glass.

lessons.title: CUF & performance ratio
lessons.summary: Measure how well a plant performs with capacity utilisation factor — calculator included.
takeaways: CUF = actual energy ÷ (capacity × hours in the period).
Indian rooftop systems typically achieve roughly 15–20% CUF.
Soiling, shading, heat and downtime reduce CUF.

lessons.title: Solar cables & ohmic losses
lessons.summary: P = I²R in action: change cable size and length and watch the losses change.
takeaways: Cable loss rises with the square of current and linearly with length.
Thicker cable (lower Ω/km) and shorter runs reduce loss.
Use solar-rated DC cable (IS 17293 / EN 50618) on the DC side.

lessons.title: MC4 connectors done right
lessons.summary: Inside a connector: why a bad crimp or a mismatched pair causes heat and arcing.
takeaways: The contact pins must seat fully with the spring clip engaged.
Crimp with the correct tool; never mate different brands unless certified compatible.
Never disconnect MC4s under load.

lessons.title: ACDB, DCDB & protection devices
lessons.summary: Where MCB, RCCB/ELCB, fuses and SPDs sit in a solar system — and what each one does.
takeaways: The DCDB protects and isolates the array side; the ACDB the grid side.
MCBs protect against over-current; RCCBs/ELCBs against earth leakage.
SPDs divert surges from lightning and switching to earth.

lessons.title: Earthing & commissioning tests
lessons.summary: An interactive commissioning checklist: continuity, voltage, earth resistance and SPD health.
takeaways: Bond inverter chassis, SPDs and module frames to the earth bar.
Earth–neutral voltage should be close to zero.
Record earth resistance — lower is better; follow the site design and IS 3043.

lessons.title: kW, kVA & power factor
lessons.summary: Drag the power factor and watch the power triangle — real vs apparent power.
takeaways: kW is real power that does work; kVA is apparent power the system must carry.
Power factor = kW ÷ kVA.
Low power factor means more current for the same useful power.

lessons.title: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
lessons.summary: Estimate the central subsidy for a residential rooftop system and the size that suits your bill.
takeaways: Residential subsidy: ₹30,000/kW for the first 2 kW, ₹18,000 for the 3rd kW, capped at ₹78,000.
GHS/RWA common facilities: ₹18,000/kW (limits apply).
Always confirm current rules on the official portal before applying.

lessons.title: Battery backup, step by step
lessons.summary: Load, capacity, depth of discharge and efficiency — build the backup estimate one step at a time.
takeaways: Battery energy (kWh) = voltage × Ah ÷ 1000.
Only part is usable: ~50% for lead-acid, ~80–90% for lithium.
Backup hours = usable energy × efficiency ÷ load.

lessons.title: Keeping a system healthy
lessons.summary: Cleaning, inspection and monitoring routines that protect yield and warranties.
takeaways: Clean gently when the glass is cool; avoid abrasive tools.
Inspect connectors, cables and earthing periodically.
Watch daily generation for sudden drops.

lessons.title: Solar myths vs facts
lessons.summary: Flip the cards — common misconceptions, answered with datasheet facts.
takeaways: Panels still produce in cloudy weather.
Heat reduces output.
DC oversizing within the inverter limit is normal.

lessons.title: Anchor by Panasonic warranty registration
lessons.summary: The four steps to register an end-customer warranty on Panasonic's portal.
takeaways: Register in the end customer's name, as on the invoice.
Upload the invoice and enter serial numbers.
Track the request ID and download the certificate online.
